def count_name_value_length_match(names, values):
    """
    You have been assigned to the records office of the Meridian Street
    distribution warehouse, where the quarterly stock reconciliation is now
    underway. During intake, every article that crosses the receiving dock
    is entered into the master ledger under two parallel registers: the
    first register holds the article's catalogue name exactly as printed on
    its shelf label, and the second holds a numeric figure transcribed by
    the clerk on duty.

    names is a list of strings and values is a list of ints of the same
    length; names[i] and values[i] describe the same item.

    Under the depot's original labelling convention, the numeric figure
    entered for an article was simply the length of its printed name, a
    practice intended to let auditors confirm at a glance that the two
    registers had not drifted apart. In later years the second register was
    repurposed for other bookkeeping figures, and the old convention fell
    out of uniform use. The audit office has therefore requested a tally of
    how many ledger entries still conform to the historical practice.

    Count the items whose value equals the number of characters of their
    name.

    The resulting tally will be entered on the reconciliation cover sheet
    and forwarded to the regional office before the close of the fiscal
    quarter, in keeping with standing warehouse procedure.

    Examples:

    >>> count_name_value_length_match([], [])
    0
    >>> count_name_value_length_match(['fig', 'cam', 'eel', 'refill', 'bolt', 'fig', 'dyn'], [26, 7, 3, 5, 4, 0, 30])
    2
    """
